title: Senior's toolkit: seeing and shaping requests
summary: curl with the flags testers use, the browser's DevTools, an intercepting proxy (Burp Suite or ZAP) and its Repeater, ZAP's baseline scan in CI, and jq to read what comes back.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: seeing and shaping requests
steps.body: Manual web testing is mostly one loop: capture a real request, change one thing, send it again, read the answer. These are the tools people use for that loop, and the scan that runs in the pipeline.

toolkit.what: Send exactly the request you mean and see the whole answer. The basis of every proof of concept in a bug report.
flags: show the status line and response headers
show your request too (lines starting with >)
put an encoded payload in the query string
pretend to come from another site

toolkit.what: Turn any request the page sent (cookies, headers, body) into a curl command you can edit and replay. Also: Application → Cookies shows HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite for each cookie; the Console shows CSP violations.
flags: keep requests across page loads and redirects
see what the server really sends
toolkit.when: the first step of reproducing any front-end bug report

toolkit.what: An intercepting proxy between the browser and the site: every request is recorded and can be edited before it is sent. Repeater resends one request with changes; Intruder sends many variations (ids 1 to 5000). Community Edition is free; OWASP ZAP is the open-source alternative with the same ideas.
flags: the same request with a list of payloads
replay every request with a second user's cookie to find IDOR
toolkit.example: Browser → proxy at 127.0.0.1:8080 → Proxy → HTTP history → right-click GET /api/orders/1001 → Send to Repeater → change 1001 to 1003 → Send

toolkit.what: OWASP ZAP's baseline scan: spider the site for a minute and report passive findings (missing headers, cookies without flags, error disclosure) without attacking it. Safe to run against staging on every deploy.
flags: set each rule to IGNORE, WARN or FAIL
do not fail the build on warnings
toolkit.example: docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/zap/wrk" -t ghcr.io/zaproxy/zaproxy:stable zap-baseline.py -t https://staging.shop.example -r zap-report.html
toolkit.when: in CI after deploying to staging; zap-full-scan.py actively attacks, so only with permission and never against production

toolkit.what: Read and filter the JSON an API returns: pull one field out of a big answer, or check a condition in a script.
flags: exit code 1 when the result is false or null: good for scripts and checks

steps.prompt: Match each flag or feature to what it does.
pairs: shows the request you sent, not only the answer
saves the cookies the server sets
puts an encoded value in the query string
edits and resends one captured request

steps.prompt: Replay a captured order request as a second user, and print only the order's owner id.
steps.explain: `-b bob.jar` sends Bob's session. If the answer is Alice's order, that is an IDOR, and two accounts are all it takes to find it.

steps.prompt: The team wants a security scan on every deploy, with no risk of damaging data. Which fits?
options: ZAP's baseline scan against staging, failing the build on chosen rules
ZAP's full scan against production every hour
Burp Intruder with a big wordlist against the login page
No scan: scanners only find false positives
steps.explain: The baseline scan is passive: it spiders and reads answers. Active scans send attack payloads that can create junk data or lock accounts, so they run with permission, against test systems.

steps.prompt: You suspect `GET /api/invoices/{id}` has an IDOR. Put the manual test in order.
lines: Sign in as user A in the browser and open one of A's invoices
Copy the request as cURL from DevTools
Sign in as user B and save B's cookies with curl -c
Send A's request with B's cookies (-b) and read the status
Write it up: the request, the response, and what B could read
